blocks.text:
PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL

Mr. Robert Grimes
General Manager
{{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}

Dear Robert,

Thank you for the time you and the shareholders have given us over the past several weeks, and for the candor with which you described both what the business needs from its balance sheet and what its owners need from the business. This letter sets out the terms on which Quillon Harbor Advisors LLC will act as financial advisor to {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} on the recapitalization we discussed, and we have tried to write it so that nothing in it promises more than a financing process can deliver.

Our work will begin on {{fact:f:E-2016-001.start}} and has a single object: to put in front of the shareholders a financing, or a clear choice between financings, that refinances the company's existing bank facility and provides the liquidity the owners have asked for, on terms the company's cash flow can carry through its slower months. To get there we will review the business plan and the monthly accounts, build a financial model that reconciles to the company's own records, and give the shareholders a written comparison of the capital structures open to them, with our recommendation. We are not engaged to raise equity or to find a buyer for the company, and if the shareholders' thinking moves in either direction we will talk with you about whether that work needs a letter of its own.

Once the shareholders have chosen a structure, we will prepare a financing memorandum, together with a short summary for first contact that describes the company by sector and revenue band only, and we will propose a list of {{fact:f:E-2016-001.scope}} for your approval before any of them is approached. We will then manage the outreach, the confidentiality agreements and the management meetings, compare the proposals that come back, recommend the lender or lenders we believe the company should proceed with, and support you and your counsel through the negotiation of the credit documents to closing.

I will lead the engagement myself and will attend every meeting with the shareholders. Robert Turner, an Associate, will manage it day to day, building the model and the memorandum and keeping the data room and the weekly agenda in order, while Sarah Fletcher, an Advisory Associate, will run the approach to financing sources and keep the contact log that records it. You will be our single point of contact at the company, which keeps the circle of people who know about the process as small as you would like it to be.

The schedule below sets out what we will deliver, in the order we expect to deliver it. The timing is indicative and counted in weeks from the start of the engagement; the later stages depend on how quickly financing sources respond, and we will tell you promptly, and in writing, if the timetable moves.

rows: Review of the business plan and monthly accounts; financial model reconciled to the company's records
Written comparison of the capital structures open to the company, with our recommendation to the shareholders
Financing memorandum; a short summary for first contact that does not name the company; data room index
Proposed list of {{fact:f:E-2016-001.scope}}, for the shareholders' approval before any approach is made
Approach to the approved sources under confidentiality agreements; management meetings; weekly contact log
Side-by-side comparison of the proposals received, and our recommendation on the lender or lenders to proceed with
Support to the company and its counsel through negotiation of the credit documents and closing

blocks.text: Fees, expenses and payment

Our fee for the engagement is {{fact:f:E-2016-001.fee}}, which we will invoice in installments: the first on signature of this letter, the second when the financing memorandum is released to financing sources, and the balance at closing of the financing. We will also bill reasonable out-of-pocket expenses, chiefly travel to lender meetings, at cost and monthly, we will ask you before incurring any expense that is out of the ordinary, and our invoices are payable within thirty days.
Term and termination

This letter takes effect when you sign it and runs until the financing closes, unless either of us ends it sooner by written notice, which either of us may do at any time. If the engagement ends before closing, the installments already invoiced are the whole of our fee, unless the company closes a financing within twelve months with a source we introduced, in which case the balance falls due at that closing; the paragraphs on confidentiality and on liability survive in any event.
Confidentiality

We will hold everything you give us in confidence and use it only for this engagement. Nothing that circulates outside the company before a financing source has signed a confidentiality agreement will name the company, which will be described by sector and revenue band alone, and the name, the memorandum and the data room will follow only once that agreement is in place.
Reliance and limitation of liability

We will rely on the information the company provides without verifying it independently, and we will not give legal, tax or accounting advice, for which the company should look to its own counsel and accountants. Our liability to the company in connection with this engagement is limited to the fees we have received under this letter, except where a loss results from our gross negligence or willful misconduct, and the company agrees to indemnify us against claims by third parties arising from the engagement, other than claims arising from that same negligence or misconduct.
Governing law

This letter is governed by the laws of the state in which our principal office is located, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules, and any dispute between us that we cannot resolve by discussion will be heard in the courts of that state.

If this letter reflects our understanding, please sign both copies and return one to me. As soon as we have it, Robert Turner will send you our initial information request, and we will hold the first working session with you in the week the engagement begins.
Accepted and agreed on behalf of {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}:

header: What we need from the company
rows: Integrated model tied to the monthly management accounts and the existing debt schedule
Monthly accounts for the last three fiscal years and year to date; current budget; the bank facility agreement
Written comparison of a senior-only financing with a senior and junior combination, with a recommendation
The shareholders' objectives on liquidity and control, gathered through Robert Grimes
Draft memorandum; data room index; short summary for first contact that does not name the company
Revenue history by customer and product line; fixed asset register; insurance and lease summaries
Proposed list of {{fact:f:E-2016-001.scope}}, grouped into senior and junior capital, for the shareholders' approval
Any lenders the shareholders want included or left out, and the history of the existing bank relationship
Weekly call agenda and decision log
A standing hour each week with Robert Grimes

blocks.text: The table above is the division of labor for the {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} recapitalization, which formally began on {{fact:f:E-2016-001.start}}, and the split follows the order in which the shareholders will have to make decisions, not the order that would be most convenient for us. Heather Delacruz owns the structure paper because the choice between senior debt alone and a senior and junior combination belongs to the shareholders, and she is the one who will put it to them. I have kept the model and the memorandum together because every figure in the memorandum has to come out of the model, and the simplest way to make sure the two never disagree is to have one person answer for both.

Sarah Fletcher takes the source list now, weeks before anyone can be called, because a good list takes that long to build and to check against what the shareholders want, and because we need to understand the existing bank's position before we decide where it sits in the order of approach. Coordination runs through Robert Grimes alone, at his request, so that information requests do not land on staff at the company who have not been told about the process. The same caution applies to us: until a source has signed a confidentiality agreement, the company is described by sector and revenue band in everything we send, including our own emails to lenders, and the name stays in the files on our side.

The sequencing constraint is easy to state and easy to lose sight of under deadline: nothing goes to any financing source until three things have happened, in this order. The model has to reconcile to the monthly accounts before the structure paper can be finished, the shareholders have to choose a structure before the memorandum can be written past the business description, and the memorandum and the list both have to be approved before Sarah makes a first call. Workstreams 3 and 4 can and should run alongside 1 and 2 up to that point, but drafts stay inside the team, and Sarah has asked me to record that a finished list is not the same thing as permission to use it.

With two Roberts on the weekly call, I will answer to Turner. What I need back, by Wednesday, is any correction to the owners or the dependencies above from each of you, and from Heather the shareholders' objectives as Robert Grimes has described them, so that the model work starts against a fixed plan.
Which capital structure should {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} take to lenders?

Since the engagement began on {{fact:f:E-2016-001.start}}, we have reconciled the model to the monthly accounts and drafted the financing memorandum as far as the business description. The memorandum cannot be finished, and no financing source can be approached, until the shareholders choose the structure we will market, because the list of {{fact:f:E-2016-001.scope}} we have prepared divides between banks and other senior lenders on one side and funds providing junior capital on the other. A decision this month keeps outreach on the timetable in our engagement letter.
Our answer: market a senior facility and a junior tranche together

items: Precedent. In the {{fact:f:E-2016-001.comparators}} we reviewed for industrial and business-services companies of similar size, senior lenders seldom went as far as the total the shareholders have in mind, and junior capital usually covered the difference.
Cash flow. The model shows cash generation weighted to the second half of the year, and the amortization a senior-only facility would require falls hardest in the months when cash is thinnest.
Cost and control. Junior capital costs more than bank debt, but it asks for little or no amortization, and on the terms we expect it can be arranged without warrants or a board seat.
The existing bank. A senior facility of conventional size leaves the existing bank room to bid, and its knowledge of the company is worth keeping in the process.
One round. Marketing both pieces at once lets each lender price against the whole structure, so the shareholders see the real trade-off between cost and covenants before they commit.

blocks.text: What we need from the shareholders to proceed

The draft memorandum and the proposed source list went to Robert Grimes with this deck, and both are written on the assumption that the recommendation is accepted. Before our working session later this month we ask the shareholders for a decision on the structure, their comments on the draft memorandum, and approval of the source list, with any additions or exclusions marked on it. Heather Delacruz will take the shareholders through the recommendation in person if that would help, Sarah Fletcher will begin first calls only once the list is approved, and questions on the model should come to Robert Turner.
Working session on the {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} recapitalization

items: Heather Delacruz, Managing Partner, Quillon Harbor Advisors
Robert Turner, Associate, Quillon Harbor Advisors
Sarah Fletcher, Advisory Associate, Quillon Harbor Advisors

blocks.text: We have put the decisions first, because they are what the shareholders asked to see. Robert Grimes confirmed, on the shareholders' behalf, that the company will take a senior facility and a junior tranche to market together, as we recommended in our briefing earlier this month, and that the existing bank will be invited to bid for the senior facility alongside the other lenders. The financing memorandum was approved for release once the two changes agreed today are made, and the financing source list was approved as presented, with first calls to begin on Monday.

Most of our time went to the junior tranche, and to the shareholders' concern, as Robert Grimes put it, that its price would come straight out of the liquidity they are seeking. We walked through the model's monthly cash flow together, and what settled the question was that the junior piece asks for very little amortization in the months when the business has the least cash to spare, which a senior-only facility of the same total could not offer; the shareholders will accept the higher price on that basis, provided we press hard on it once proposals arrive.

The two changes to the memorandum came from the shareholders' wish to say as little as possible before a lender has committed to the process. They asked that the largest customers be described by industry and length of relationship, not by name, until a lender has signed a confidentiality agreement and met management, and that the section on the existing bank facility say less about its history, and Robert Turner will make both changes. Sarah Fletcher then took us through the order of approach, with senior lenders first and junior funds a few days behind them and every first call describing the company by sector and revenue band only, and we agreed that the existing bank should hear about the process from us before it hears about it from anyone else.

We closed on the timetable. Robert Turner confirmed that releasing the memorandum as the first confidentiality agreements come back keeps outreach within the weeks our engagement letter set aside for it, and Robert Grimes asked that the management meetings be grouped so that the shareholders give up as few working days as possible, which Sarah Fletcher will build into her calls from the start.

items: Robert Turner: make the two agreed changes to the financing memorandum, load the final version to the data room, and confirm to Robert Grimes that both are done before first calls begin on Monday.
Heather Delacruz: call the existing bank's relationship manager this week, so that the bank hears about the process, and its invitation to bid, from us directly.

Sarah Fletcher: begin first calls to the approved financing sources on Monday using the summary that does not name the company, send the confidentiality agreement to any source that asks for more, and keep the contact log current for the weekly call.
Robert Grimes: hold time in September for management meetings with lenders, and send the July monthly accounts as soon as they are closed.
All of us: our regular weekly call, at which Sarah Fletcher will report on the first week of outreach.

blocks.text: Status Report for {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}: Release of the Memorandum and the First Week of Outreach

This report is for Robert Grimes and covers the period from the August working session, at which the shareholders settled the structure and approved the memorandum and the source list, to the end of last week. Measured against the schedule in our engagement letter, the work is on plan: the diagnostic, the structure recommendation and the financing memorandum are complete, the memorandum and the data room were ready for release when the first confidentiality agreements came back, and first calls began on the Monday after the session, as agreed.

Sarah Fletcher's contact log now shows {{fact:f:E-2016-001.pipeline-lenders-approached}} since first calls began. Senior lenders were called first and junior funds a few days later, every first call described the company by sector and revenue band only, and the name, the memorandum and the data room have gone only to sources that have signed a confidentiality agreement. No source has had a management meeting yet, which is where the plan expects us to be at this point, and we are arranging the first of them over the next three weeks.

Two pieces of preparation for that stage are in hand. The management presentation that you and the shareholders will give at lender meetings is in draft, built from the memorandum so that every figure in it matches, and it will come to you for comment this week; the data room follows the index agreed in July, and the July monthly accounts were added as soon as they arrived. Once the management meetings are complete, we will ask every source that remains interested for a written proposal by a common date, so that the shareholders can compare price, structure and covenants side by side, not one proposal at a time.

The approved source list stands at {{fact:f:E-2016-001.scope}} and we do not propose to widen it yet. Nothing we have heard on first calls contradicts the pricing and leverage ranges we drew from the {{fact:f:E-2016-001.comparators}} reviewed in July, though first calls are a poor guide to price and we will not lean on them until written proposals arrive. On cost, the engagement is within budget: the fee of {{fact:f:E-2016-001.fee}} set in our engagement letter is unchanged, the second installment was invoiced on release of the memorandum as the letter provides, and expenses so far are limited to travel for the August session.

items: R1. Junior appetite. Owner: Sarah Fletcher. Trigger: if no junior fund has asked for a management meeting by the end of next week, we come back to the shareholders with names to add to the junior side of the list.

R2. Current trading. Owner: Robert Grimes. Trigger: if the August accounts show margin below the model's forecast, we restate the model and tell every source in the data room before any of them reaches a management meeting.

R3. Existing bank payoff. Owner: Heather Delacruz. Trigger: if the bank has not confirmed its payoff terms in writing by the time the first proposals arrive, we ask the company's counsel to obtain them directly.

R4. Management time and confidentiality inside the company. Owner: Robert Grimes. Trigger: if a lender asks for a site visit during working hours, we hold it early in the day or off site and keep the company's attendees to the people who already know.

R5. Timetable. Owner: Robert Turner. Trigger: if management meetings cannot be completed within the next three weeks, the date for written proposals moves, and we reissue the timetable to every source on the same day.

blocks.text: The risk picture has shifted since the last report, which was written before the shareholders' decision. The choice of structure has closed, and R3 has narrowed from whether the existing bank would cooperate at all to the paperwork of its payoff, since Heather Delacruz called the bank before outreach began and it has said it will bid for the senior facility. R1 and R4 are new, and both became real only once first calls started; R2 and R5 are carried forward from the last report as they stood.

Of the five, R2 is the one we can get ahead of, because the model can be checked against actual results before any lender sees a revised figure. To do that I need the August monthly accounts from you by Friday, so that we can rerun the model before the first management meeting is confirmed.
